body:
An unneeded sequel that proves to be as good as the first !

After surviving one deadly game, Grace and her sister Faith must now outrun four rival families competing for a powerful throne - winner takes all.

The movie is surprisingly well, not a total blow for blow of the first one but same premise with different antics. The acting all round was good and having Graces sister kept it feeling fresh.

There were some nice surprises in the story, good kills, good tactics. The only thing that genuinely bothered me was the gun scenes, nobody shoots that bad and if you have a gun faced to the bad guy, SHOOT.

Overall good movie, I say it will be the last, great ending, 8/10.

I was thoroughly enjoying this sequel, that is up until the 3rd act. The way the story wraps up was predictable and a bit too tidy. It just didn't make a lot of sense with the main character and it cut the suspense and unpredictable nature the film had going for it. As soon as the revelation is made, you know exactly how the film is going to end.

The acting this time around is more of the same, but the sisters dynamic made for an interesting beat that skewed the trope the first movie relied heavily on. Not only did the main character have to be a badass, but she also had to be a caring person. I find it a bit hard to believe Grace never said anything about having a sister when getting married into such a wealthy and guarded family but suspension of disbelief is easy for this kind of film.

The film wasn't quite as hard hitting with the kills as it was in the first, albiet it was quite a bit more violent. On the other hand, there is quite a bit more of the exploding bodies in this one and it made for some fun set pieces.

The main problem with the kills in this film is we aren't given enough to hold onto the families trying to retain their positions in the world. Practically, all of them are reprehensible characters with little to no reedemable qualities. In the first film we spend more time with the family and getting to know each character as an individual. The people in this sequel were all stereotypical bad people. The film makes you want to hate them and see them killed in the worst fashions.

Again though, with the way it all ends up, I expected more of a fight and less of the seriousness the film plays for. The way the first film ends was fun and cheeky. This one felt more like the writers wrote themselves into a corner and went with a more conventional ending as opposed to the hilarious ironic ending of the first film.

Overall, I enjoyed it, even with the predictable 3rd act revelation. It had interesting sibling dynamics and a good amount of tension when watching the sisters fight for their lives. I just wished the writers had thought a little more out of the box as opposed to the loophole contract they played for.

3 black weddings out of 5.

Ready or Not 2: Here I Come is a watchable but unnecessary follow-up to a film that didn't really need one. The first movie worked because it was tight, surprising, and knew when to stop. This one doesn't quite have that discipline.

There's plenty to enjoy. The cast is strong across the board, with names like Sarah Michelle Gellar and Elijah Wood adding real presence, and the performances help carry the film through its weaker moments. There are also a lot of funny bits, and the film leans further into the gore, sometimes to the point of excess.

Where it struggles is pacing. It drags more than it should, easily fifteen to twenty minutes too long, and the added lore, while interesting at first, never quite justifies the runtime. Expanding the world takes away some of the simplicity that made the original so effective.

It's still watchable and has its moments, but it feels like a clear step down from the first.

The second secret screening of the week was, as was widely predicted "Ready or Not 2: Here I Come". I missed the first film at the cinema but caught it at home afterwards. I enjoyed that, and this sequel, though it never quite reached the levels of fun I was hoping for.

Having survived the night in the Le Domos house, Grace (Samara Weaving) is taken to hospital where her estranged sister Faith (Kathryn Newton) is called as her next of kin. From the hospital, the girls are drugged and taken to the estate of the Danforth Family, where a lawyer (Elijah Wood) explains to them that having survived the night, Grace has trigged a new game where a whole group of rich and powerful families will hunt Grace and, if they can land the killing blow, they will become the new head of their global cabal.

One of my criticisms of the first film was that I didn't feel the casting for the rest of the family were particularly strong. That's not the case here as the cast includes, Sarah Michelle Gellar, David Cronenberg, Kevin Durand and Nestor Carbonell - though perhaps it's most daring casting move is to bring Shawn Hatosy back to the big screen after so many years doing - admittedly really good- work on TV. He's (unsurprisingly) really good. It's Weaver's film again though and she is a fantastic scream queen and great alongside Kathryn Newton.

Whilst the film is undoubtably alright, my only real issue is that it never quite hit the level of fun I was looking for consistently enough. It does get there occasionally though.

Personally, I don't think there's enough there to mine for a third film ( "you can't hide") but as ever financial success, or lack thereof, will dictate that.

I just got out of Ready or Not 2: Here They Come.

I found the first movie to be really entertaining and enjoyable (was it really 2019??), so I was looking forward to this.

Sadly this is nowhere near as good, as the first movie. Which is surprising given it's the same writers, director and main star of the first movie.

It's simply a remake of that movie, but not as good and more complicated. I know they were trying to expand on the lore and build on it, but it feels like a Ready or Not rip off, rather than a sequel.

Of the cast Samara Weaving is again excellent as Grace!! She alone, is worth seeing this movie for, no phoning it in for the sequel, here. Kathryn Newton is a good addition as Grace's sister Faith, but I very quickly got tired over them repeatedly squabbling about the state of their relationship. Elijah Wood is always reliable, Sarah Michelle Geller is the biggest stand out of the supporting cast, Shawn Hatosy is solid and I always enjoy seeing Kevin Durand pop up on screen.

It was too comedic in tone as the hunters were incompetent to say the least, which led to it losing most of its dramatic tension.

I feel like I'm bashing it too much, but I didn't hate it, it has some good, fun and clever moments, but over all it's just a sloppy, convoluted rehash of the first movie, when I was hoping for much better.
